  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Manchester < Old English Mameceaster; Mame < Celtic *mamm- (breast, hill) + ceaster (Roman fort); Arena < Latin harena (sand, sandy place)",
    "reading": "Fort on the breast-shaped hill; sand-strewn place of contest",
    "languages": ["en", "la", "cel"],
    "source": "Oxford English Dictionary; Lewis & Short Latin Dictionary",
    "confidence": 0.8
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "Man + chester + arena; man (human) + chester (chest, from Latin castra? but homophone of chest) + arena (sand)",
    "reading": "Man's chest of sand — a hollow breast filled with grit, a stage for breath",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.6
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "Manchester → manche (Fr: sleeve) + ster (Fr: sterile? no, ster from Greek stereos solid); Arena → arène (Fr) → arène = sand; also 'manche' = handle",
    "reading": "Handle of solid sand — a grip that dissolves, a tool of the void",
    "languages": ["fr", "en", "grc"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",
    "chain": "Manchester Arena → 'a rare man's centre' + 'h' + 'e'? Better: 'arcane master' + 'hen'? Let's take 'arcane' + 'men' + 'heart' + 's'",
    "reading": "Arcane men's heart — a hidden core within the public circle",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "notariqon",
    "chain": "M-A-R-E-A → M (mater, mother) + A (a, without) + R (rex, king) + E (est, is) + A (arena, sand) → 'mater a rex est arena'",
    "reading": "Mother without king is sand — the feminine ground rules over the crowned",
    "languages": ["la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "letter_symbol",
    "chain": "M (12th letter, water in alchemy) + A (1, beginning) + R (18, fire) + E (5, spirit) + A (1) — sequence 12-1-18-5-1",
    "reading": "Water, beginning, fire, spirit, beginning — a cycle of elements in a sandy bowl",
    "languages": ["en", "la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "numerical",
    "chain": "Manchester Arena → sum of letters (A=1...Z=26): M13+A1+N14+C3+H8+E5+S19+T20+E5+R18 = 106; Arena: A1+R18+E5+N14+A1 = 39; total 145",
    "reading": "145 = 1+4+5=10, the perfect number — a place of completion and return to unity",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "Man + chester + arena; chester → 'chest' + 'er' (one who) → one who chests; arena → 'air' + 'ena' (Greek: one) → air one",
    "reading": "Man who chests the air — a breather in a sandy ring, a lung of the crowd",
    "languages": ["en", "grc"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  }
]
